children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose more than 1% on Wednesday to close at the highest level since late July, on gains led by chip and battery makers.
closed 97.12 points or 1.40%higher, at 7,051.64, its highest closing level since July 23.
** "Investor sentiment is recovering around AI infrastructure investments," said Huh Jae-hwan, an analyst at Eugene Investment Securities.
** OpenAI said in a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday that it was deepening cooperation with Samsung Electronics across semiconductors and enterprise AI services.
** U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in a letter to Ford Motor
CEO Jim Farley sent on Tuesday said the automaker's dealings with Chinese battery makers raised "profound concern" and urged the automaker to cut ties.
** Of the total 913 traded issues, 463 shares advanced, while 400 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 435.0 billion won ($325.57 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,336.1 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.50% higher than its previous close at 1,342.8.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.05 point to 103.06.
